data.description:
## Story

As a release engineer running the post-migration audit for `## Closure Checks`, I can run a source-file consumer audit that scans `.md`, `.sh`, `.py`, `.yaml`, `.yml` files in `plugins/`, `tests/`, `docs/` to identify every place in the codebase that references the Closure Checks schema — so pointer updates can land per bucket recipe across consumer files until the audit reaches steady state (zero unflagged matches or explicit RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE).

This story re-implements epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 SC4 and SC5 at the full scope specified in the epic. The existing `audit-closure-checks-migration.sh` (a ticket-body scanner) is **not** the SC4/SC5 implementation — it solved a different problem (ticket migration target identification). This story builds the source-file consumer audit that SC4 actually specifies.

## Done Definitions (verbatim from epic SC4 + SC5)

- DD1 (SC4 — script): A new script (proposed path `plugins/dso/scripts/audit-closure-checks-source-consumers.sh` to avoid name collision with the existing ticket-body audit) implements the combined methodology over `.md`, `.sh`, `.py`, `.yaml`, `.yml` files in `plugins/`, `tests/`, `docs/`.

- DD2 (SC4 — pattern sweep): Pattern sweep includes (a) variable-interpolation hints — match shell-style interpolations like `$VAR='Closure Checks'`, Python f-strings `f"...Closure Checks..."`, YAML keys/values mentioning the section; (b) aliases — match `closure-chk`, `cc-items`, and any other shorthand discoverable via grep over the existing codebase; (c) section-name regex — match `## Closure Checks` with whitespace tolerance.

- DD3 (SC4 — reverse-dependency enumeration): Follows static imports (Python `import`/`from`, shell `source`, markdown `[link](path)` references) AND flags dynamic loads — `importlib.import_module(variable)`, `$PLUGIN_ROOT`/`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`-rooted sourcing, indirect path computation. Dynamic loads are flagged because they cannot be resolved statically; the audit must surface them for manual review.

- DD4 (SC4 — classification buckets): Each match is assigned to one of six buckets. Bucket schema documented in script header:
  - `section-name-reference` — literal `## Closure Checks` heading or its aliases
  - `file-path-reference` — references to files known to consume the schema (e.g., `migrate-closure-checks.sh`, `audit-closure-checks-migration.sh`)
  - `semantic-consumer` — code that parses or generates the section content (completion-verifier Step 2.5, coherence-walk.sh, etc.)
  - `test-asserting-on-structure` — test files that assert on the section's presence or shape
  - `user-facing-copy` — error messages, log output, documentation prose that mentions the section to end users
  - `migration-in-progress` — temporary references introduced by migration tooling (e.g., transitional comments)

- DD5 (SC4 — JSON output): Output written to `plugins/dso/.audit-output/closure-checks-migration-<timestamp>.json` with schema `{audit_run_id, started_at, file_count_scanned, buckets: { <bucket-name>: [{file, line, match_text, dynamic_load: bool}] }, dynamic_load_count, unbucketed_matches: [...]}`. Directory created if absent; existing artifacts not overwritten.

- DD6 (SC4 — reconciliation): After first pass, the script runs up to 4 additional reconciliation passes (5 total) — each pass re-scans only files modified since the previous pass's completion. Convergence: a pass completes with zero new bucket flags. Non-convergence after 5 iterations: emit `RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE` block listing residual flags to stdout AND `reconciliation_status: "incomplete"` in JSON output.

- DD7 (SC5 — pointer updates land): Pointer updates land across consumer files identified by DD1–DD6 per bucket recipe. Recipe definitions (to be drafted during implementation-plan):
  - `section-name-reference`: literal heading already migrated; flagged matches are remaining stale references in copy or comments → rewrite or remove
  - `file-path-reference`: paths verified extant; if path moved, update reference
  - `semantic-consumer`: code that reads the section is verified to read from the new location; tests added for backward-compat
  - `test-asserting-on-structure`: tests updated to assert on the new schema (`## Closure Checks` heading present + items conform to one-shot-verifiable per SC9)
  - `user-facing-copy`: prose updated to mention the new section name
  - `migration-in-progress`: removed when migration completes

- DD8 (SC5 — steady state): Re-running the audit returns zero unflagged matches OR `RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE` with documented residual reasons. Both outcomes are acceptable; the contract is that the steady-state signal is unambiguous.

← Validates Closure Check: "audit-closure-checks-source-consumers.sh exists at plugins/dso/scripts/ and runs without error in CI"
← Satisfies: "SC4: audit-closure-checks-migration.sh implements combined methodology over .md, .sh, .py, .yaml, .yml files in plugins/, tests/, docs/. Pattern sweep includes variable-interpolation hints (e.g., $VAR='Closure Checks'), aliases (closure-chk, cc-items), and section-name regex. Reverse-dependency enumeration follows static imports AND flags dynamic loads (importlib.import_module with variable, $PLUGIN_ROOT-rooted sourcing). Six classification buckets: section-name-reference, file-path-reference, semantic-consumer, test-asserting-on-structure, user-facing-copy, migration-in-progress. Output: structured JSON to plugins/dso/.audit-output/closure-checks-migration-<timestamp>.json. Reconciliation pass terminates after max 5 iterations with remaining flags surfaced as RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE."
← Satisfies: "SC5: Pointer updates land per bucket recipe across consumer files identified by SC4. Re-running the audit script returns zero unflagged matches OR an explicit RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE block listing residuals (steady state)."

## Considerations

- **Name collision with existing script**: the existing `plugins/dso/scripts/audit-closure-checks-migration.sh` solves a different problem (ticket-body migration target identification). Two acceptable resolutions: (a) rename the existing script to `audit-ticket-closure-checks.sh` to free the SC4 name, OR (b) name the new script `audit-closure-checks-source-consumers.sh`. Implementation-plan should pick one and document.
- **Bucket-classifier logic ambiguity**: when a match could belong to multiple buckets (e.g., a test file with user-facing error copy), the classifier picks the most specific bucket. Document tie-breaking rules in the script header.
- **`.audit-output/` directory**: confirm this is gitignored before adding outputs (audit artifacts are run-specific, not source).
- **Reconciliation convergence**: the "files modified since previous pass" check requires capturing a mtime baseline at first-pass start. Implementation-plan should pick a stable mechanism (git index-aware vs. raw mtime).

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked — agents proceed unless a significant assumption is required that could send implementation in the wrong direction. All assumptions made without escalating are documented.
data.title: As a release engineer, run a source-file consumer audit for Closure Checks with six bucket classification and reconciliation
